stg.customers.name: customer_id
stg.customers.description: CRM customer number. Repeats once per version of the record.

stg.customers.name: first_name
stg.customers.description: Given name as keyed in the CRM.

stg.customers.name: last_name
stg.customers.description: Family name as keyed in the CRM.

stg.customers.name: date_of_birth
stg.customers.description: Date of birth; age is a protected attribute.

stg.customers.name: address_line1
stg.customers.description: First line of the postal address.

stg.customers.name: county
stg.customers.description: County as keyed (spelling and case vary). Can act as a proxy for protected attributes.

stg.customers.name: eircode
stg.customers.description: Irish postcode, with or without the space.

stg.customers.name: marketing_opt_in
stg.customers.description: Y or N; NULL when never asked.

stg.customers.name: customer_since
stg.customers.description: Date the person first became a customer.

stg.customers.name: source_system
stg.customers.description: Channel that created the record (CRM, WEB, BROKER).

stg.customers.name: updated_at
stg.customers.description: When this version of the record was written.

stg.customers.name: _row_seq
stg.customers.description: Position of the row in the extract file.

contracts.grain: One row per CRM customer (customer_id), taken from one version of the customer's CDC records saved on or before @AsOfDate.

columns.name: initials
columns.description: SUBSTRING(x,0,2) in T-SQL returns only the first character, so this is the first letter of first_name plus the first letter of last_name, in upper case.

columns.name: email_shared_count
columns.description: Number of kept customer rows with the same email. 0 when email is NULL.

columns.name: age_at_join
columns.description: DATEDIFF(YEAR) from date_of_birth to customer_since. This counts calendar-year boundaries crossed, not completed years of age.

columns.name: region
columns.description: Sales region looked up from county. Counties not in the list, and NULL counties, get UNKNOWN.

columns.name: eircode_valid
columns.description: Checks length only: Y when the length is 7, or 8 with a space in position 4. T-SQL LEN ignores trailing spaces.

columns.name: is_standard_segment
columns.description: Y only when segment_code = 'STD'. segment_code is CHAR(4), so it is padded to 'STD '; T-SQL ignores trailing spaces when comparing, Spark does not.

columns.name: version_count
columns.description: Number of CDC versions of the customer saved on or before @AsOfDate.

columns.name: record_updated_at
columns.description: updated_at of the version that was kept. ROW_NUMBER orders by updated_at and _row_seq ascending and keeps version_no = 1, so this is the EARLIEST version, not the current one the header describes. The migration must copy this behaviour.

columns.name: as_of_date
columns.description: The @AsOfDate parameter. It is the same on every row.

cases.description: County values in the wrong case for every region list (DUBLIN, cork, GALWAY, donegal, LAOIS), a segment_code of 'std', and emails that differ only in case (Mary@x.ie / mary@x.ie / MARY@X.IE). Under the CI collation the legacy job puts each county in its region, flags 'std' as standard, and counts the three emails as one shared address (3). A naive Spark translation sends the counties to UNKNOWN, flags 'std' as N, and counts each email as 1. One canonical row (Dublin, STD) is included for comparison.

County values with trailing spaces for every region list ('Dublin ', 'Cork ', 'Mayo ', 'Sligo ', 'Offaly '). Emails that differ only by a trailing space ('pat@x.ie' and 'pat@x.ie '). segment_code values 'STD' (stored padded as 'STD ' in CHAR(4)) and 'PR' (padded to 'PR  '). SQL Server ignores trailing spaces, so it matches the counties to their regions, counts the shared email as 2, flags STD as Y and returns segment_code padded to 4 characters. A naive Spark translation gets UNKNOWN regions, counts 1 for each email, flags the padded 'STD ' as N, or returns an unpadded segment_code.

Builds full_name and initials with + from first_name and last_name. Both columns are NOT NULL in stg.customers, so a NULL can't be loaded and the NULL case of the trap is latent. The rows cover the edge cases that are allowed: an empty first name, an empty last name, and names with trailing spaces, which are concatenated after RTRIM. On these rows a concat() translation and the legacy job should give the same full_name and initials, and a concat_ws() translation that skips empty or NULL parts would differ only if a NULL could reach it.

Names that give 2-letter initials in T-SQL, because SUBSTRING(x,0,2) returns only the first character. A naive Spark substring(x,0,2) returns 2 characters per name, so it gives 4-letter initials. The Eircodes include trailing spaces: 'D02X285 ' and 'D02X2851  ' have a T-SQL LEN of 7 and 8, and 'D02 X285 ' has a LEN of 8 with a space at position 4. T-SQL's LEN ignores trailing spaces, so it marks some of these valid where a naive length() would not. Canonical codes ('D02X285', 'D02 X285') and an invalid code ('D02X28') are included.

Birth dates and join dates where counting year boundaries (DATEDIFF YEAR) gives a different age than counting full years elapsed. Examples: born 1990-12-31 and joined 2020-01-01 (boundaries 30, full years 29), and born 1985-06-15 and joined 2015-06-14. A row where a birthday has already passed in the join year, and a row with no date of birth (NULL age), are included as controls.
